questions.question: Reliability focuses on continuing correct operation when:
options: Everything is healthy and load is zero in real production systems at scale.
Things go wrong — machines, networks, processes, humans.
You disable all monitoring to avoid alert fatigue.
You reject every request before it touches business logic.
questions.explanation: continuing to work correctly, even when things go wrong

reference.excerpt: continuing to work correctly, even when things go wrong

questions.question: Xu’s rate limiter fault-tolerance requirement says if the limiter/cache fails:
options: The entire site must go offline until cache returns in real production systems at scale.
Problems with the rate limiter should not take down the whole system.
All users must be permanently banned automatically in real production systems at scale.
DNS should return NXDOMAIN for the marketing site in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: If there are any problems with the rate limiter… it does not affect the entire system

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: If there are any problems with the rate limiter… it does not affect the entire system

questions.question: Redundancy helps availability because:
options: One server failure can be absorbed by another taking over.
Identical bugs on all replicas magically cancel out.
You can delete backups once two servers exist in real production systems at scale.
Load disappears when you double the number of machines.
questions.explanation: When one fails, another one can take over

reference.excerpt: When one fails, another one can take over

questions.question: True or false: High availability is often expressed as “nines” of uptime in an SLA.
questions.explanation: Uptime is traditionally measured in nines. The more the nines, the better

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: Uptime is traditionally measured in nines. The more the nines, the better

questions.question: Retries without idempotency are dangerous because:
options: Networks never duplicate or delay packets in practice in real production systems at scale.
Duplicate side effects (double charge, double notify) can occur.
HTTP forbids clients from ever resending a request in real production systems at scale.
Queues delete messages before workers can see them always.
